hee_001: You can recognise it by its wide, layered crown, lower limbs thickened after two centuries of outward growth. It stands in the woodland north of Imstenrade.
hee_002: You can recognise it by its lopsided crown, open on the side that faced the forest edge and crowded on the other. It stands at the edge of the trees north of Nieuw Eyckholt.
hee_003: You can recognise it by its open, rounded crown, grown with pavement and front doors around it rather than other trees. It stands where Markiesstraat meets three other streets.
hee_006: You can recognise it by being a plane despite its local name, the Oak of Terworm, its wide low crown standing alone at a junction. It stands near the Eikendermolenweg.
hee_007: You can recognise it by its leaves squared off at the tip as if cut with scissors, and flowers facing upward high in the crown. It stands in the park along Baron Mackaystraat.
hee_008: You can recognise it by standing beside the drive up to Kasteel Terworm, visible to anyone approaching the front door, near an old yew. It stands at Terworm 5D.
hee_009: You can recognise it by the bench built around its base and the steel props holding up a swing hung from one limb. It stands outside Heerlen's town hall.
